sentences.en: Today, every mass shooting in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 今天，美国发生的每一场大规模枪击事件，

sentences.en: is inevitably followed by a call for gun control.
sentences.zh: 都不可避免地引发了对枪支管控的呼吁。

sentences.en: But it never happens.
sentences.zh: 但这种情况从未发生过。

sentences.en: The story behind why the legislation always fails and the NRA always wins.
sentences.zh: 这背后的故事是：为什么立法总是失败，而美国全国步枪协会（NRA）总是获胜。

sentences.en: And a gun shop owner talks about putting military-style weapons into the hands of civilians.
sentences.zh: 此外，一位枪店老板谈到了将军事风格武器交到平民手中的问题。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, October 4th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月4日，星期三。

sentences.en: Robert, take me back to the early decades of the NRA.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特，带我回顾一下NRA成立初期的几十年。

sentences.en: What role did the
sentences.zh: 当时，

sentences.en: National Rifle Association play in American culture?
sentences.zh: 全国步枪协会在美国文化中扮演了什么角色？

sentences.en: Well, originally, its role in American culture was purely recreational.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最初它在美国文化中的角色纯粹是娱乐性的。

sentences.en: Robert Draper has reported on the NRA for the Times magazine.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·德雷珀曾为《时报》杂志报道过NRA。

sentences.en: It was founded in 1871 basically as a means of teaching former Union soldiers how to be hunters, how to use their firearms to eat and to recreate.
sentences.zh: 它成立于1871年，基本上是为了教退伍的联邦士兵如何成为猎人，如何利用枪支来获取食物和进行娱乐。

sentences.en: So it's a hunting group, essentially.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上它是一个狩猎组织。

sentences.en: It was a hunting group for basically 120 years.
sentences.zh: 它基本上做了120年的狩猎组织。

sentences.en: It wasn't until the 1960s that that began to change with social unrest that led to the Gun Control Act of 1968.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪60年代，随着社会动荡导致了1968年《枪支管制法》的出台，这种情况才开始改变。

sentences.en: The burning of our churches will not deter us.
sentences.zh: 焚烧我们的教堂不会阻挡我们。

sentences.en: The farming of our homes will not dissuade us.
sentences.zh: 耕种我们的家园不会劝阻我们。

sentences.en: The beating and killing of our clergymen and young people will not divert us.
sentences.zh: 殴打和杀害我们的神职人员和年轻人不会让我们偏离方向。

sentences.en: The wet and release of their known murderers will not discourage us.
sentences.zh: 释放那些已知的杀人犯不会让我们灰心。

sentences.en: We're on the move now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正在行动。

sentences.en: Glory, hallelujah.
sentences.zh: 荣耀，哈利路亚。

sentences.en: It's also worth remembering, Michael, that during that period of the 1960s were the assassinations of John F.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，还要记住，在20世纪60年代那一时期，发生了约翰·F·

sentences.en: Kennedy, Martin Luther King, and Robert F.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪、马丁·路德·金和罗伯特·F·

sentences.en: Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪的遇刺事件。

sentences.en: The notion of guns being real agents of violence was a really resonant one at that point in American life.
sentences.zh: 枪支是真正的暴力工具这一观念，在当时的美国生活中引起了强烈的共鸣。

sentences.en: From Dallas, Texas, the flash, apparently official, President Kennedy died at 1 p.m.
sentences.zh: 来自德克萨斯州达拉斯的快讯，据官方消息，肯尼迪总统于下午1点去世。

sentences.en: Central Standard Time,
sentences.zh: 中部标准时间，

sentences.en: 2 o'clock Eastern Standard Time, some 38 minutes ago.
sentences.zh: 东部标准时间2点，也就是大约38分钟前。

sentences.en: Today we begin to disarm the criminal and the careless and the insane.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们开始解除罪犯、粗心者和精神失常者的武装。

sentences.en: And it was in that atmosphere in 1968 that Congress and President Johnson acted to pass the gun control legislation of 1968.
sentences.zh: 正是在1968年这种氛围下，国会和约翰逊总统采取行动，通过了1968年的枪支管制立法。

sentences.en: And some of you may be interested in knowing really what this bill does.
sentences.zh: 你们中有些人可能想知道这项法案到底做了什么。

sentences.en: Which imposed stringent restrictions really for the first time on the ability to purchase firearMs.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是第一次对购买枪支的能力施加了严格的限制。

sentences.en: It stops murder by mail order.
sentences.zh: 它阻止了邮购谋杀。

sentences.en: It bars the interstate sale of all guns and the bullets that load them.
sentences.zh: 它禁止了所有枪支及其弹药的州际销售。

sentences.en: It stops the sale of lethal weapons to those too young to bear their terrible responsibility.
sentences.zh: 它停止了向那些太年轻而无法承担可怕责任的人出售致命武器。

sentences.en: We have come a long way.
sentences.zh: 我们已经走过了很长一段路。

sentences.en: We have made much progress, but not near enough.
sentences.zh: 我们取得了很大进步，但还远远不够。

sentences.en: So how does the NRA, as a gun club, mostly focused on hunting, get involved in that?
sentences.zh: 那么，作为一个主要专注于狩猎的枪支俱乐部，NRA是如何卷入其中的呢？

sentences.en: What happened after that was that one of its most active members, Congressman John Dingell,
sentences.zh: 在那之后发生的事情是，它最活跃的成员之一，国会议员约翰·丁格尔，

sentences.en: I'd like to begin with congratulations to Mr. Thomas and his staff for the successful negotiations.
sentences.zh: 我想首先祝贺托马斯先生及其团队谈判成功。

sentences.en: Began to sound the alarm that perhaps there would be even more restrictions coming down the pike.
sentences.zh: 开始敲响警钟，称未来可能会有更多的限制措施出台。

sentences.en: So Dingell began to talk to other NRA members and said,
sentences.zh: 于是丁格尔开始与其他NRA成员交谈，并说：

sentences.en: Look, we've got to quit acting just like sportsmen.
sentences.zh: 听着，我们不能再表现得像个运动员了。

sentences.en: If we're not careful, our firearms and the ability of what firearms we're able to have left will be severely curtailed.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不小心，我们的枪支以及我们还能拥有的枪支能力将受到严重削减。

sentences.en: We need essentially to develop our own lobbying organization.
sentences.zh: 我们本质上需要发展自己的游说组织。

sentences.en: We need to push back.
sentences.zh: 我们需要反击。

sentences.en: Thanks to you, the members and supporters of NRA, no national gun law has passed this year.
sentences.zh: 感谢你们，NRA的成员和支持者，今年没有通过任何全国性的枪支法律。

sentences.en: And it was really under that climate that a legislative lobbying organization of the NRA was founded in 1975.
sentences.zh: 正是在这种气候下，NRA的立法游说组织于1975年成立。

sentences.en: It is not likely at this time that one will pass if we will stand together shoulder to shoulder for what is right.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能肩并肩为正义而战，现在不太可能通过这样的法律。

sentences.en: And on top of that, They were able to vote out the former leadership, which was suspected of having gone soft on the gun control issue.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，他们成功投票罢免了前任领导层，因为后者被怀疑在枪支管制问题上立场软化。

sentences.en: The more mild-mannered, hunting-oriented leadership of the NRA were ousted that very same year.
sentences.zh: NRA中那些温和的、以狩猎为导向的领导层在同一年被赶下台。

sentences.en: And replaced with Second Amendment absolutists, who began to employ the language of the slippery slope.
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是第二修正案的绝对主义者，他们开始使用“滑坡谬误”的语言。

sentences.en: If you take my rifles, my shotguns, and my pistols away from me, are you going to take the bullies and arrows too?
sentences.zh: 如果你拿走我的步枪、猎枪和手枪，你是不是也要拿走我的弓箭？

sentences.en: That one law would surely be followed by another law.
sentences.zh: 这一项法律肯定会被另一项法律所取代。

sentences.en: And then what are you going to do then after that?
sentences.zh: 那在那之后你打算做什么？

sentences.en: Take the pocket knives, the hunting knives?
sentences.zh: 拿走折叠刀、猎刀吗？

sentences.en: You know, where's the stopping you going?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你打算在哪里停下来？

sentences.en: And before you knew it, essentially all guns would be collected and taken away from Americans.
sentences.zh: 在你意识到之前，基本上所有的枪支都会被收集并从美国人手中夺走。

sentences.en: So it was really the first time that we saw the NRA start to develop its political muscle.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是我们第一次看到NRA开始展现其政治影响力。

sentences.en: And in particular, that began to take place in 1986.
sentences.zh: 特别是，这种情况始于1986年。

sentences.en: There are four minutes remaining.
sentences.zh: 还剩四分钟。

sentences.en: When it passed the Gun Ownership Protection Act.
sentences.zh: 当时它通过了《枪支所有权保护法》。

sentences.en: And the bill is passed and the motion of reconsideration is laid upon.
sentences.zh: 法案获得通过，重新审议的动议被搁置。

sentences.en: Again, led by an NRA member and influential congressman, John Dingell, a Democrat of Michigan.
sentences.zh: 同样，由NRA成员、有影响力的国会议员、密歇根州民主党人约翰·丁格尔领导。

sentences.en: Congress set out to reverse what they believed were a lot of the deleterious provisions in the 1968 Gun Control Act.
sentences.zh: 国会着手推翻他们认为1968年《枪支管制法》中许多有害的条款。

sentences.en: An act to protect firearms owners' constitutional rights, civil liberties, and rights to privacy.
sentences.zh: 一项旨在保护枪支所有者宪法权利、公民自由和隐私权的法案。

sentences.en: So it was a win all the way around for the NRA, except one bone was thrown to gun control people.
sentences.zh: 所以这对NRA来说是一场全面的胜利，除了给枪支管制支持者扔了一根骨头。

sentences.en: One thing was agreed to by the NRA, and that's that machine guns be banned.
sentences.zh: NRA同意了一件事，那就是禁止机枪。

sentences.en: There was the belief that, look, this is such a win overall.
sentences.zh: 当时有一种信念，看，这总体上是一场巨大的胜利。

sentences.en: We are getting so much in return that really no one's going to care that much about machine guns.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了这么多回报，真的没人会那么在意机枪。

sentences.en: And yet, it developed that people did hold a grudge against the NRA for giving in.
sentences.zh: 然而，事实证明，人们确实因为NRA的让步而对它怀恨在心。

sentences.en: For giving in on this, for just this one provision of the law on machine guns.
sentences.zh: 因为在这一点上，仅仅因为法律中关于机枪的这一条规定而让步。

sentences.en: Why was that such a big deal for people inside the NRA?
sentences.zh: 为什么这对NRA内部的人来说是一件大事？

sentences.en: If you accept them purely on their own terms, they really do believe that the right to bear arms should not be abridged by any kind of legislation.
sentences.zh: 如果你完全按照他们自己的逻辑来接受他们，他们确实认为持有武器的权利不应受到任何形式立法的限制。

sentences.en: And so the notion of compromise is one that they say should not exist with a constitutionally sanctioned right.
sentences.zh: 因此，妥协的概念在他们看来是不应该存在于宪法保障的权利之中的。

sentences.en: Right, because from the outside, it seems easy to say, how are we debating background checks or selling guns to mentally ill people?
sentences.zh: 没错，因为从外部来看，说“我们怎么还在争论背景调查或向精神病患者出售枪支”似乎很容易。

sentences.en: Because these seem to many people like no-brainers as far as regulation goes.
sentences.zh: 因为在许多人看来，这些在监管方面是显而易见的。

sentences.en: But they're saying at the NRA, look, this is just a pure constitutional matter.
sentences.zh: 但NRA的人说，看，这纯粹是一个宪法问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, they're saying something else too, Michael, which is that the people who are saying, hey, all we want to do, we're not trying to take away people's guns.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，他们还说了另一件事，那就是那些说“嘿，我们只想做点什么，我们不是想夺走人们的枪支”的人，

sentences.en: We just want to be sensible with gun control legislation by, for example, closing loopholes in background checks.
sentences.zh: “我们只是想通过例如填补背景调查中的漏洞来制定明智的枪支管制立法。”

sentences.en: The argument that the NRA will often make to that is, let's take a closer look at the sincerity of those individuals who are saying that this is really all they want to do.
sentences.zh: NRA对此通常提出的论点是，让我们仔细看看那些声称这确实是他们唯一想做的人的诚意。

sentences.en: And at this point, the NRA will point to legislators such as Democratic Senator Dianne Feinstein from California, who has said on more than one occasion that, in fact,
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，NRA会指出像加利福尼亚州民主党参议员黛安·范斯坦这样的立法者，她不止一次地说过，事实上，

sentences.en: if she could muster the votes to ban firearms, then she would do so.
sentences.zh: 如果她能争取到足够的选票来禁止枪支，她就会这样做。

sentences.en: If I might pose a question to the senior senator from California,
sentences.zh: 如果我可以向加利福尼亚州的高级参议员提一个问题，

sentences.en: would she deem it consistent with the Bill of Rights for Congress to engage in the same endeavor that we are contemplating doing with the Second Amendment in the context of the First or Fourth Amendment?
sentences.zh: 她是否认为国会参与我们正在考虑对第二修正案所做的同样努力，在第一或第四修正案的背景下符合权利法案？

sentences.en: Namely,
sentences.zh: 即，

sentences.en: would she consider it constitutional for Congress to specify that the First Amendment shall apply only to the following books and shall not apply to the books that Congress has deemed outside the protection of the Bill of Rights?
sentences.zh: 她是否认为国会规定第一修正案仅适用于以下书籍，而不适用于国会认为在权利法案保护范围之外的书籍是符合宪法的？

sentences.en: Senator, I've been on this committee for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 参议员，我在这委员会待了20年。

sentences.en: I was a mayor for nine years.
sentences.zh: 我当了九年市长。

sentences.en: I walked in, I saw people shot.
sentences.zh: 我走进去，我看到了被枪杀的人。

sentences.en: I've looked at bodies that have been shot with these weapons.
sentences.zh: 我见过被这些武器射杀的尸体。

sentences.en: I've seen the bullets that implode.
sentences.zh: 我见过会爆炸的子弹。

sentences.en: In Sandy Hook, youngsters were dismembered.
sentences.zh: 在桑迪胡克，孩子们被肢解了。

sentences.en: Look, there are other weapons.
sentences.zh: 看，还有其他武器。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In other words, give them an inch.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，给他们一寸，

sentences.en: It feels like the NRA is saying.
sentences.zh: 感觉NRA是这么说的。

sentences.en: And those who are trying to limit what can be sold will take a mile.
sentences.zh: 那些试图限制销售内容的人就会进一尺。

sentences.en: So we've got to double down.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须加倍努力。

sentences.en: We give nothing.
sentences.zh: 我们什么都不给。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Clearly, they're not interested in remediating a particular problem, except insofar as, in their view, the problem is guns being in existence in America.
sentences.zh: 显然，他们对解决特定问题不感兴趣，除非在他们看来，问题本身就是枪支在美国的存在。

sentences.en: This does not prohibit.
sentences.zh: 这并不禁止。

sentences.en: You use the word prohibit.
sentences.zh: 你用了“禁止”这个词。

sentences.en: It exempts 2,271 weapons.
sentences.zh: 它豁免了2,271种武器。

sentences.en: Isn't that enough for the people in the United States?
sentences.zh: 这对美国人民来说还不够吗？

sentences.en: Do they need a bazooka?
sentences.zh: 他们需要火箭筒吗？

sentences.en: Do they need other high-powered weapons that military people use to kill in close combat?
sentences.zh: 他们需要军人在近距离战斗中用来杀人的其他高威力武器吗？

sentences.en: I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我不这么认为。

sentences.en: So this seems like a good moment to talk about how the NRA reacts when there are mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 所以这似乎是一个谈论NRA在发生大规模枪击事件时如何反应的好时机。

sentences.en: Potentially, these are spasms of gun violence that could be the single biggest threat to the NRA, the most likely time you'd expect the organization to give an inch.
sentences.zh: 潜在地，这些枪支暴力的痉挛可能是对NRA最大的威胁，也是你最可能期望该组织让步的时候。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, there is a time-honored playbook by the NRA after mass shootings, and we've seen this since Columbine in 1999.
sentences.zh: 嗯，NRA在大规模枪击事件后有一套久经考验的剧本，自1999年科伦拜事件以来我们已经看到了这一点。

sentences.en: Describe that scene in...
sentences.zh: 描述一下那个场景……

sentences.en: Well, me and my friend Chris were just out during lunch, and we heard what sounded like firecrackers, and so we looked over,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我和我的朋友克里斯午餐时刚出来，我们听到了听起来像鞭炮的声音，所以我们看过去，

sentences.en: and we saw some guys with guns creeping around a corner.
sentences.zh: 我们看到几个拿着枪的人在拐角处潜行。

sentences.en: He looked at us, and then he started shooting at us, and so we, like, fell to the ground.
sentences.zh: 他看着我们，然后开始向我们射击，所以我们就像倒在了地上。

sentences.en: We're back on the air now with another update for you on the Columbine High School shooting in Littleton, Colorado.
sentences.zh: 我们现在回到直播，为您带来科罗拉多州利特尔顿科伦拜高中枪击事件的最新消息。

sentences.en: If you were just joining us,
sentences.zh: 如果您刚加入我们，

sentences.en: two young men apparently dressed in long black trench coats opened fire about an hour and a half ago at a high school just outside of Denver in Littleton, Colorado.
sentences.zh: 两名身穿黑色长风衣的年轻人大约一个半小时前在丹佛郊外科罗拉多州利特尔顿的一所高中开火。

sentences.en: At least three students have been injured, and possibly as many as eight.
sentences.zh: 至少有三名学生受伤，可能多达八人。

sentences.en: We know that victims have been taken to the hospital...
sentences.zh: 我们知道受害者已被送往医院……

sentences.en: Joining us now, NBC News correspondent Dan Abrams, who has just arrived in Littleton.
sentences.zh: 现在加入我们的是NBC新闻记者丹·艾布拉姆斯，他刚刚抵达利特尔顿。

sentences.en: Dan, what can you tell us?
sentences.zh: 丹，你能告诉我们什么？

sentences.en: It's an eerie sight to see so many sort of scenes from an everyday school event.
sentences.zh: 看到这么多日常学校活动的场景，真是一种诡异的景象。

sentences.en: You see kids walking around in gym attire.
sentences.zh: 你看到孩子们穿着健身服走来走去。

sentences.en: You see students still working out with their weight belts on, but you see a lot of tears.
sentences.zh: 你看到学生们仍然系着举重腰带在锻炼，但你看到了很多泪水。

sentences.en: Perhaps now America would wake up to the dimensions of this challenge, and we could prevent anything like this from happening again.
sentences.zh: 也许现在美国会意识到这一挑战的规模，我们就能防止类似的事情再次发生。

sentences.en: The first thing they do is a seemingly nothing, which is to remain silent.
sentences.zh: 他们做的第一件事是看似什么都不做，那就是保持沉默。

sentences.en: Our words and our behavior will be scrutinized more than ever this morning.
sentences.zh: 今天早上，我们的言行将受到比以往任何时候都更严格的审视。

sentences.en: Those who are hostile towards us will lie in wait to seize on a soundbite out of context, ever searching for an embarrassing moment to ridicule us.
sentences.zh: 那些对我们怀有敌意的人会伺机而动，断章取义地抓住一段录音，不断寻找尴尬的时刻来嘲笑我们。

sentences.en: Knowing that any statement is probably not going to do any good, could, in fact, do more harm than good.
sentences.zh: 因为知道任何声明可能都不会有任何好处，实际上可能弊大于利。

sentences.en: What they will be doing instead during that period is checking to see what the political headwinds are, hearing whatever feedback they may be getting from, say, Republican leaders.
sentences.zh: 他们在此期间会做的是检查政治风向，听取他们可能从共和党领导人那里得到的任何反馈。

sentences.en: If they begin to say to them, for example, this is going to be tough for us to just stay silent on, we may actually have to consider some legislation.
sentences.zh: 如果他们开始对他们说，例如，这对我们来说很难保持沉默，我们可能真的需要考虑一些立法。

sentences.en: Then the NRA begins to go into action, but it does so quietly at firSt.
sentences.zh: 那么NRA就开始采取行动，但起初是悄悄地进行。

sentences.en: The first step is to mount a membership drive,
sentences.zh: 第一步是发起会员招募活动，

sentences.en: to send out newsletters saying your Second Amendment rights are under attack yet again by a disingenuous Congress that wants to take away your firearMs.
sentences.zh: 寄出时事通讯，声称你们的宪法第二修正案权利再次受到一个虚伪国会的攻击，他们想要夺走你们的枪支。

sentences.en: Never fight if you can avoid it.
sentences.zh: 如果能避免，就永远不要去战斗。

sentences.en: But when you must fight, don't lose.
sentences.zh: 但当你必须战斗时，绝不能输。

sentences.en: And when nothing less than freedom is at stake, we fight.
sentences.zh: 而当事关自由，我们必须战斗。

sentences.en: We're millions of people just like you.
sentences.zh: 我们有数百万像你一样的人。

sentences.en: We're the longest standing civil rights organization in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们是美国历史最悠久的民权组织。

sentences.en: Proud defenders of history's patriots.
sentences.zh: 历史爱国者们引以为傲的捍卫者。

sentences.en: Protectors of the Second Amendment.
sentences.zh: 第二修正案的守护者。

sentences.en: Advocating the right to keep and bear arMs.
sentences.zh: 倡导持有和携带武器的权利。

sentences.en: Advancing the shooting sports.
sentences.zh: 推动射击运动的发展。

sentences.en: The upshot of this will be that they will be able to recruit new members and in turn have more membership dues in their war cheSt.
sentences.zh: 这样做的结果是，他们能够招募新成员，进而让他们的战争基金里有更多的会费。

sentences.en: And with this war chest, they can then initiate a lobbying campaign against members of Congress.
sentences.zh: 有了这笔战争基金，他们就可以发起针对国会议员的游说运动。

sentences.en: First, to do all they can to halt any legislation in its tracks.
sentences.zh: 首先，尽其所能阻止任何立法进程。

sentences.en: And then secondly, to basically threaten legislators who intend to vote for the legislation so that they will not do so.
sentences.zh: 其次，基本上是威胁那些打算投票支持该立法的议员，让他们不敢投赞成票。

sentences.en: And the senators generally are themselves convinced that it is a battle that they do not wish to fight.
sentences.zh: 参议员们通常自己也确信，这是一场他们不想打的仗。

sentences.en: And they don't say so on the record, but they have certainly said that to me unattributed.
sentences.zh: 他们不会在公开记录中这么说，但他们确实私下对我这样说过。

sentences.en: It happens like that.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: The police can't get there in time.
sentences.zh: 警察无法及时赶到。

sentences.en: How you defend yourself is up to you.
sentences.zh: 如何保护自己取决于你自己。

sentences.en: It's your choice.
sentences.zh: 这是你的选择。

sentences.en: But Mary Landrieu voted to take away your gun rights.
sentences.zh: 但玛丽·兰德里投票支持剥夺你的持枪权。

sentences.en: Vote like your safety depends on it.
sentences.zh: 投票吧，就像你的安全取决于它一样。

sentences.en: Defend your freedom.
sentences.zh: 捍卫你的自由。

sentences.en: Defeat Mary Landrieu.
sentences.zh: 击败玛丽·兰德里。

sentences.en: The NRA Political Victory Fund is responsible for the content of this advertising.
sentences.zh: 美国全国步枪协会（NRA）政治胜利基金对本广告内容负责。

sentences.en: Robert, is this an actual playbook, what you're describing that the NRA is using?
sentences.zh: 罗伯特，你所描述的NRA正在使用的，是一套真正的剧本吗？

sentences.en: Is this more or less a codified strategy?
sentences.zh: 这是否算是一套成文的策略？

sentences.en: No, it's not written down, but it's so understood and has been repeated over and over with such success.
sentences.zh: 不，它没有写下来，但大家都心照不宣，而且反复使用并取得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: Beginning in 1999, because after Columbine, Bill Clinton tried to pass a background checks bill.
sentences.zh: 始于1999年，因为在科伦拜恩枪击案之后，比尔·克林顿试图通过一项背景调查法案。

sentences.en: But it happened that the president was still recovering from the Monica Lewinsky scandals in 1999.
sentences.zh: 但当时的情况是，总统在1999年仍未从莫妮卡·莱温斯基丑闻中恢复过来。

sentences.en: He was really no match for the power of the NRA.
sentences.zh: 他确实无法与NRA的力量抗衡。

sentences.en: And so whatever political capital he had just simply wasn't enough.
sentences.zh: 所以他拥有的任何政治资本都根本不够用。

sentences.en: And the bill never made it out of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 该法案最终没能走出参议院。

sentences.en: And so that was a success for the NRA.
sentences.zh: 所以这对NRA来说是一次胜利。

sentences.en: And it becomes, as you said, a strategy that they use after every mass shooting going forward.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这成为了他们此后在每次大规模枪击事件后都会使用的策略。

sentences.en: Yes, that continued to be the case after the shootings at Virginia Tech in 2007.
sentences.zh: 是的，在2007年弗吉尼亚理工大学枪击案之后，情况依然如此。

sentences.en: Later, after the 2012 Newtown massacre, all of these were cases where there was a sentiment, particularly from the progressive side of the spectrum,
sentences.zh: 后来，在2012年纽敦镇大屠杀之后，所有这些案例中，人们都有一种情绪，特别是进步派阵营，

sentences.en: that surely now there would be sensible gun control legislation.
sentences.zh: 认为现在肯定会有合理的枪支管制立法了。

sentences.en: And when it did not eventuate, each time it did not eventuate, the legend of the NRA, as it were, began to grow.
sentences.zh: 而当它没有实现时，每一次都没有实现时，NRA的传奇色彩就开始增长了。

sentences.en: Their power seemed to be that much more unassailable for every obstacle that they were able to surmount.
sentences.zh: 他们每克服一个障碍，他们的力量似乎就变得更加不可动摇。

sentences.en: So ironically, as these mass shootings continue and in some ways become worse, they strengthen the National Rifle Association.
sentences.zh: 所以讽刺的是，随着这些大规模枪击事件持续发生，甚至在某些方面变得更糟，它们反而加强了全国步枪协会。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: No, and in fact, it is historically the case that the NRA's membership has gone down when there isn't some kind of galvanizing moment for them.
sentences.zh: 不，事实上，从历史上看，当没有某种激励他们的时刻时，NRA的会员人数反而会下降。

sentences.en: Whether that galvanizing moment is a Democratic president, the prospect of a Democratic president, or a shooting that spurs legislation largely by Democratic legislators.
sentences.zh: 无论那个激励时刻是民主党总统、民主党总统候选人，还是由民主党议员推动立法的枪击事件。

sentences.en: So yes, in a very twisted, perverse sense, these kinds of tragedies actually help grow the power of the NRA.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，从一种非常扭曲、反常的角度来看，这些悲剧实际上有助于壮大NRA的力量。

sentences.en: So to go back to the 1960s and bring this full circle,
sentences.zh: 回到20世纪60年代，把这一切串联起来，

sentences.en: an organization that became politicized in the first place in response to the assassinations of these giant figures like Martin Luther King and Robert Kennedy solidified power in response to these modern mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 一个最初为了回应马丁·路德·金和罗伯特·肯尼迪等巨人遇刺而政治化的组织，在应对这些现代大规模枪击事件中巩固了权力。

sentences.en: Yes, the NRA as we know it today really came into being as a direct result of violence in America and legislators' attempts to do something about that violence.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们今天所知的NRA确实是美国暴力事件以及立法者试图解决这些暴力事件的直接结果。

sentences.en: Before then, the NRA was a quiet, not-so-large organization mainly devoted to hunting.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，NRA是一个安静的、规模不大的组织，主要致力于狩猎。

sentences.en: The NRA as we know it today is an NRA that was born out of the violence, gun violence, in America.
sentences.zh: 我们今天所知的NRA，是一个诞生于美国暴力，即枪支暴力中的NRA。

sentences.en: Thank you, Robert.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，罗伯特。

sentences.en: Really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: My pleasure, Michael.
sentences.zh: 不客气，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Hey, is this John?
sentences.zh: 嘿，是约翰吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Michael Barbaro from The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: Okay, Ben.
sentences.zh: 好的，本。

sentences.en: John, can you tell me about your store?
sentences.zh: 约翰，你能跟我说说你的店吗？

sentences.en: Maybe just describe it to me.
sentences.zh: 也许可以给我描述一下。

sentences.en: You're talking about the gunshot?
sentences.zh: 你说的是枪击案吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I decided I didn't want to sell the same thing they did, which was all hunting equipment.
sentences.zh: 我决定不卖他们卖的东西，也就是那些狩猎装备。

sentences.en: And so I started out by selling, like, an AR-15.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始卖像AR-15这样的枪。

sentences.en: John Merkel owns a gun store in Roanoke, Virginia, that sells military-style weapons.
sentences.zh: 约翰·默克尔在弗吉尼亚州罗阿诺克拥有一家枪店，出售军用风格的武器。

sentences.en: Oh, they're sexy.
sentences.zh: 哦，它们很迷人。

sentences.en: Beautiful woman.
sentences.zh: 美丽的武器。

sentences.en: They're all extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 它们都非同寻常。

sentences.en: So here's a question that I've been wondering about, knowing that I would be talking to you.
sentences.zh: 所以有一个问题我一直很好奇，既然知道要和你谈话。

sentences.en: I feel like I understand why people buy handguns, and I also understand why people buy hunting rifles to hunt.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我理解为什么人们买手枪，我也理解为什么人们买猎枪去打猎。

sentences.en: But I feel like I don't understand as well why people buy these kind of higher-powered guns.
sentences.zh: 但我感觉我不太理解为什么人们会买这种高威力的枪。

sentences.en: And it sounds like you carry some of those weapons.
sentences.zh: 听起来你确实有卖这些武器。

sentences.en: Oh, I carry a lot of them, but you can't even hunt with them.
sentences.zh: 哦，我有很多，但你甚至不能用它们打猎。

sentences.en: But why do people buy that sort of gun?
sentences.zh: 那人们为什么要买那种枪呢？

sentences.en: Oh, just for fun.
sentences.zh: 哦，只是为了好玩。

sentences.en: That's all.
sentences.zh: 仅此而已。

sentences.en: Just for, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 只是为了，你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Do you have any idea how much fun it is to take for even 500?
sentences.zh: 你知道玩这个有多开心吗，哪怕是500发子弹？

sentences.en: So what you're describing is kind of sport, not for hunting, not for self-defense.
sentences.zh: 所以你描述的是一种运动，不是为了狩猎，也不是为了自卫。

sentences.en: No, just sport.
sentences.zh: 不，只是运动。

sentences.en: It's more for sport than for any other reason.
sentences.zh: 比起任何其他原因，它更多是为了运动。

sentences.en: We simply have fun with them.
sentences.zh: 我们只是玩得很开心。

sentences.en: So when someone buys a gun like that, is that what you imagine they're doing with it?
sentences.zh: 所以当有人买那样的枪时，你想象他们就是这样用的吗？

sentences.en: For the most part, yes.
sentences.zh: 大部分情况下，是的。

sentences.en: John, what's the process?
sentences.zh: 约翰，流程是什么样的？

sentences.en: If I walk into a store, me, Michael Barbarnoff, and I want to buy an assault rifle or something like a machine gun, what happens?
sentences.zh: 如果我走进一家店，我，迈克尔·巴巴罗，想买一把突击步枪或者像机关枪之类的东西，会发生什么？

sentences.en: What happens is we size the person up.
sentences.zh: 会发生的是，我们会评估这个人。

sentences.en: Do you have any idea how much sales we've lost just because we refused to sell the gun?
sentences.zh: 你知道我们因为拒绝卖枪而损失了多少销售额吗？

sentences.en: Something didn't smell right.
sentences.zh: 感觉有些不对劲。

sentences.en: We get lots of mad people.
sentences.zh: 我们遇到过很多愤怒的人。

sentences.en: I mean, we've seen some really squirrely people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们见过一些真的很古怪的人。

sentences.en: We just felt so, we just didn't feel right.
sentences.zh: 我们只是觉得，就是感觉不对。

sentences.en: But nothing other than a feeling to go on.
sentences.zh: 但除了感觉之外，没有别的依据。

sentences.en: And how often does that happen?
sentences.zh: 这种情况多久发生一次？

sentences.en: Weekly?
sentences.zh: 每周？

sentences.en: Monthly?
sentences.zh: 每月？

sentences.en: I mean, it's ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: It literally probably cost me $20,000.
sentences.zh: 这实际上可能让我损失了2万美元。

sentences.en: But so say I pass the kind of John visual teSt.
sentences.zh: 但假设我通过了约翰的目测测试。

sentences.en: They're going to do two, say yes.
sentences.zh: 他们会做两次，说可以。

sentences.en: And does that take some time?
sentences.zh: 那需要花些时间吗？

sentences.en: Two-thirds, it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 三分之二的情况，不需要。

sentences.en: So it sounds like I could walk out with an assault rifle on the same day.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来我可以在同一天带着突击步枪离开。

sentences.en: 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 15分钟。

sentences.en: Because it's not the weapon.
sentences.zh: 因为问题不在武器。

sentences.en: The weapon's a tool.
sentences.zh: 武器只是工具。

sentences.en: No different than an axe.
sentences.zh: 和斧头没什么两样。

sentences.en: I mean, it's how you use it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关键在于你怎么使用它。

sentences.en: I sold a gun.
sentences.zh: 我卖过一把枪。

sentences.en: I mean, I wish I hadn't.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我真希望我没卖。

sentences.en: The woman committed suicide.
sentences.zh: 那个女人自杀了。

sentences.en: And she did it in our parking lot.
sentences.zh: 她就在我们的停车场里做的。

sentences.en: Because she said she didn't want her children to find her.
sentences.zh: 因为她说她不想让她的孩子们发现她。

sentences.en: I didn't want to sell it, but I did sell it.
sentences.zh: 我不想卖，但我还是卖了。

sentences.en: And didn't make any money on it.
sentences.zh: 而且我没从那笔生意里赚到钱。

sentences.en: I just felt bad for her because of the story she gave me.
sentences.zh: 我只是因为她告诉我的故事而为她感到难过。

sentences.en: She said, people have been moving into her neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 她说，有人搬进了她的社区。

sentences.en: There's gunfire at night.
sentences.zh: 晚上有枪声。

sentences.en: I'm scared to death to leave my mind if it was there.
sentences.zh: 如果我在那里，我会吓得要死。

sentences.en: She said, how do you operate this gun?
sentences.zh: 她说，这把枪怎么操作？

sentences.en: I can't make it work.
sentences.zh: 我弄不明白。

sentences.en: So they showed her.
sentences.zh: 所以他们演示给她看。

sentences.en: She went right outside and committed suicide.
sentences.zh: 她直接走出去就自杀了。

sentences.en: It turns out she was bipolar and was off her meds.
sentences.zh: 结果发现她患有双相情感障碍，而且停药了。

sentences.en: John, does it, does it, this is a difficult question.
sentences.zh: 约翰，这，这，这是一个很难的问题。

sentences.en: You may not think it's fair, but did you feel guilty after, after she did that?
sentences.zh: 你可能觉得不公平，但在她做完那件事后，你感到内疚吗？

sentences.en: And obviously with each other when she was buying the gun.
sentences.zh: 显然在买枪的时候他们彼此之间也是这样。

sentences.en: I do want to ask you about 2007.
sentences.zh: 我确实想问你关于2007年的事。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about the gun that you sold on March 13th?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我关于你在3月13日卖出的那把枪吗？

sentences.en: The Glock 19.
sentences.zh: 那把格洛克19。

sentences.en: Yeah, to Sung Wee Cho.
sentences.zh: 是的，卖给赵承熙。

sentences.en: The clerk said, the way he described it, it was a typical colleague.
sentences.zh: 店员说，按照他的描述，那是一个典型的大学生。

sentences.en: When did you first hear about the shooting, the Virginia Tech shooting?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候第一次听说那场枪击案，弗吉尼亚理工大学枪击案的？

sentences.en: Well, it happened on a Monday.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是发生在周一。

sentences.en: It was 10.
sentences.zh: 当时是10个人。

sentences.en: It just kept going up and up.
sentences.zh: 数字一直在往上涨。

sentences.en: And I kept thinking, my God, it's got to stop.
sentences.zh: 我一直在想，天哪，这得停下来。

sentences.en: We didn't know it was us until ATF told us it was.
sentences.zh: 直到烟酒枪炮及爆炸物管理局（ATF）告诉我们，我们才知道是我们卖的。

sentences.en: And the only reason they knew is because he kept the receipt in his backpack.
sentences.zh: 他们知道的唯一原因是他把收据留在了背包里。

sentences.en: They brought that receipt directly to us, the practice ammo.
sentences.zh: 他们直接把那张收据带给了我们，还有练习用的弹药。

sentences.en: It was breaking my heart.
sentences.zh: 这让我心碎。

sentences.en: My daughter graduated from Tech in 1997.
sentences.zh: 我女儿1997年从理工大学毕业。

sentences.en: I mean, I can't believe it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: It sounds like it was painful for you to realize.
sentences.zh: 听起来意识到这一点对你来说很痛苦。

sentences.en: It was painful.
sentences.zh: 很痛苦。

sentences.en: It was terribly painful.
sentences.zh: 非常痛苦。

sentences.en: I was hurt.

sentences.en: You have no idea.
sentences.zh: 你根本无法想象。

sentences.en: I don't know what to use it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该怎么用它。

sentences.en: I do want to see people use it to kill animals for eating.
sentences.zh: 我确实想看到人们用它来猎杀动物作为食物。

sentences.en: You don't kill if you don't eat it.
sentences.zh: 如果不吃它，就不要杀它。

sentences.en: And one shot, one kill.
sentences.zh: 而且要一枪毙命。

sentences.en: I gave up killing because of an incident where I did not kill a deer on the first shot.
sentences.zh: 我放弃狩猎是因为有一次我没能一枪打死一只鹿。

sentences.en: It took two.
sentences.zh: 开了两枪。

sentences.en: And that poor deer had to suffer for 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 那只可怜的鹿足足受了10分钟的罪。

sentences.en: I didn't want that.
sentences.zh: 我不想那样。

sentences.en: You're describing a feeling of guilt when a living thing is shot.
sentences.zh: 你描述的是射杀活物时产生的负罪感。

sentences.en: I don't like any living thing.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢任何活物。

sentences.en: That negates it from the NRA.
sentences.zh: 这让它与美国全国步枪协会（NRA）的理念背道而驰。

sentences.en: And one of the pages in it is just nothing.
sentences.zh: 其中一页什么内容都没有。

sentences.en: People they love.
sentences.zh: 他们所爱的人。

sentences.en: I understand what you're saying, which is that guns can be used to defend and protect as much as, in your mind, as they can be used to hurt and to damage.
sentences.zh: 我明白你的意思，你是说在你看来，枪支既可以用来伤害和破坏，也可以用来防御和保护。

sentences.en: But does what happened at Virginia Tech weigh on your conscience because your gun shop sold the gun to the shooter?
sentences.zh: 但弗吉尼亚理工大学枪击案发生后，你的良心会受到谴责吗？因为你的枪店把枪卖给了凶手。

sentences.en: Does that mean that there's something wrong with the background testing system with the law?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着背景调查系统或法律存在问题？

sentences.en: Well, reporting to the background, there's nothing wrong with the FBI doing a great job of that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，说到背景调查，联邦调查局（FBI）做得非常出色，并没有什么问题。

sentences.en: That's not the problem.
sentences.zh: 问题不在这里。

sentences.en: The problem is enough people aren't reporting these things.
sentences.zh: 问题在于没有足够多的人去举报这些情况。

sentences.en: Now, he should have been reported by at least four people.
sentences.zh: 当时至少有四个人应该举报他。

sentences.en: Because of his behavior.
sentences.zh: 因为他的行为。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Two of the two teachers and at least one student.
sentences.zh: 两名老师和至少一名学生。

sentences.en: And I don't know why people keep forgetting that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么人们总是忘记这一点。

sentences.en: John, after you went through that, selling that gun, your shop to Cho, and then hearing about the Virginia Tech shooting, did you keep your gun store open?
sentences.zh: 约翰，在经历了这一切，把那把枪卖给赵承熙，然后听说弗吉尼亚理工大学枪击案之后，你还继续经营你的枪店吗？

sentences.en: Is that something you thought about, whether to keep it open?
sentences.zh: 你有没有考虑过是否要继续开下去？

sentences.en: I just had to.
sentences.zh: 我只能继续。

sentences.en: So, after that shooting, the Virginia Tech case, did gun sales actually go up at your shop?
sentences.zh: 那么，在那次枪击案，也就是弗吉尼亚理工大学案件之后，你店里的枪支销量真的增加了吗？

sentences.en: By a factor of 10.
sentences.zh: 增加了十倍。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I want to ask you, John, about the period since Virginia Tech.
sentences.zh: 约翰，我想问问你关于弗吉尼亚理工大学事件之后的那段时期。

sentences.en: Every time there's a mass shooting, and there are mass shootings now many times a year in the United States.
sentences.zh: 现在美国每年都会发生多次大规模枪击事件。

sentences.en: Let's take the examples of what happened in Orlando or what just happened in Las Vegas.
sentences.zh: 我们以奥兰多或刚刚发生的拉斯维加斯事件为例。

sentences.en: I want to understand what goes through your mind.
sentences.zh: 我想了解你当时的想法。

sentences.en: The Times reports that Stephen Paddock, the shooter who killed at least 59 people in Las Vegas on Sunday night, used multiple semi-automatic rifles.
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》报道称，周日晚在拉斯维加斯杀害至少59人的枪手斯蒂芬·帕多克使用了多支半自动步枪。

sentences.en: Weapons that fire a single round with each pull of the trigger.
sentences.zh: 这种武器每扣动一次扳机只能发射一颗子弹。

sentences.en: At least one of those rifles was outfitted with a device that would enable it to fire hundreds of rounds per minute.
sentences.zh: 其中至少有一支步枪加装了装置，使其每分钟能发射数百发子弹。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, the Supreme Court held opening arguments in the first case of its new session, a debate over partisan gerrymandering in Wisconsin,
sentences.zh: 周二，最高法院举行了新一届会议的首个案件的开庭辩论，议题是威斯康星州的党派选区划分问题，

sentences.en: where Republicans drew the state's voting districts to give themselves a lopsided advantage in legislative elections.
sentences.zh: 共和党人在那里重新划分了选区，以便在立法选举中获得压倒性优势。

sentences.en: During the hearing, Justice Anthony Kennedy, considered the crucial vote in the case,
sentences.zh: 在听证会上，被视为该案关键一票的安东尼·肯尼迪大法官，

sentences.en: asked questions that indicated he could join the four more liberal justices in ruling that the courts can determine when lawmakers have gone too far in drawing those voting districts.
sentences.zh: 提出的问题表明，他可能会加入四位更自由派大法官的行列，裁定法院有权判定立法者在划分选区时是否做得太过火。

sentences.en: After weeks of frustration about the pace of federal relief efforts in Puerto Rico, President Trump spent four hours on the island on Tuesday and addressed its residents directly.
sentences.zh: 在对波多黎各联邦救灾工作进展缓慢感到数周沮丧后，特朗普总统周二在岛上停留了四个小时，并直接向当地居民发表了讲话。

sentences.en: Every death is a horror,
sentences.zh: 每一条生命的逝去都是一场悲剧，

sentences.en: but if you look at a real catastrophe like Katrina and you look at the tremendous hundreds and hundreds and hundreds of people that died and you look at what happened here with really a storm that was just totally overpowering.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看像卡特里娜飓风那样真正的灾难，看看那成百上千人死亡的惨状，再看看这里发生的事情，这确实是一场威力巨大的风暴。

sentences.en: Nobody's ever seen anything like this.

sentences.en: You can be very proud of all of your people, all of our people working together, 16 versus literally thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 你们可以为所有共同努力的人民感到自豪，16人对比成千上万的人。

sentences.en: Trump spoke to the recovery work of the federal government.
sentences.zh: 特朗普谈到了联邦政府的恢复工作。

sentences.en: Now, I hate to tell you, Puerto Rico, but you've thrown our budget a little out of whack.
sentences.zh: 抱歉要告诉你，波多黎各，你们让我们的预算有点失衡了。

sentences.en: And at one stop, he handed out supplies, tossing rolls of paper towels into a crowd and distributing flashlights.
sentences.zh: 在其中一站，他分发物资，把成卷的纸巾扔向人群，并分发手电筒。
